Class PingPongManager

java.lang.Object
it.polimi.ingsw.network.utils.PingPongManager
public class PingPongManager extends Object
Manages a PING/PONG heartbeat for a single TCP connection. ── Logic ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Every PING_INTERVAL_MS milliseconds the scheduler fires: 1. If awaitingPong is still true (previous ping was never answered) → TIMEOUT. 2. Otherwise: set awaitingPong = true and call sendPing.run(). When the remote peer sends a PONG back, call receivedPong() to reset the flag. When the remote peer sends a PING, call receivedPing(sendPong) to reply immediately. ── Usage (server-side handler or client) ────────────────────────────────── HeartbeatManager hb = new HeartbeatManager(); hb.start( () -> sendMessage(PING), // called every interval () -> handleDisconnect("timeout") // called once on timeout ); // on PONG received: hb.receivedPong(); // on PING received: hb.receivedPing(() -> sendMessage(PONG)); // on clean close: hb.stop();

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start(Runnable sendPing, Runnable onTimeout)
      Starts pinging. Must be called exactly once per connection lifetime.
      Parameters:
      sendPing - called every PING_INTERVAL_MS to emit a PING
      onTimeout - called once when the remote peer misses a PONG

    • receivedPong

      public void receivedPong()
      Call this when a PONG message is received. Resets the awaiting flag so the next interval doesn't timeout.

    • receivedPing

      public void receivedPing(Runnable sendPong)
      Call this when a PING message is received. Immediately invokes sendPong so the remote peer's heartbeat doesn't timeout.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the heartbeat. Call on clean disconnection to avoid the onTimeout callback firing after the socket has already been closed intentionally.
